overview: Black plays 2...f5 against the French centre and White takes 3.exf5 with a pawn up. Black answers 3...Nf6, aiming for ...d5, ...Bd6 and a kingside attack, while White develops with Nc3, Bd3 and Nf3 and can return the pawn to ease the pressure. Black has weakened the king and is playing for development; it is a surprise weapon.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nc3, Nf3, Bd3 and castle, keeping the extra pawn
Hit the Black centre with d4 and e5 or Bb5+ ideas

black_ideas.idea: Aim pieces at the white king and recapture on f5 when possible

typical_structures.structure: French-type centre with d4 against ...d5 and an extra White f5 pawn
Open e-file and f-file with weakened Black king

character.notes: Black's king is weakened by the early ...f5; play is open and relies on quick development.

gambit.notes: 2...f5 3.exf5 gives up a pawn and White can keep it.

soundness.notes: Strong players consider 2...f5 dubious; White just develops and keeps the extra pawn.

structure.notes: The d4/d5 French centre with an open e-file after captures.

approach.notes: Strong players almost never play 2...f5 in the French. Chosen for surprise.

level.notes: A dubious line that is not a good repertoire choice.

character.reason: Black's early ...f5 invites tactics on the kingside and e-file.

gambit.reason: Black gives up a pawn with 2...f5 that White can keep.

soundness.reason: Weakens the king and gives a pawn for little compensation.

structure.reason: d4 against ...d5 with an open e-file after captures, not yet fully open.

level.reason: Dubious, so never Beginner; little theory to learn.

plans.reason: Black plays for rapid development after giving the pawn.
